subject: ventures/cash-runway-planner
professional: a small-business bookkeeper or fractional CFO who builds 13-week cash-flow forecasts for service businesses. First checks: does the weekly roll-forward add up, does the forecast start from the receivables already outstanding, and is the advice it gives (move this bill, chase that invoice) actually true when you apply it.

evidence.correctness: The weekly roll-forward is right. An independent Python recomputation (/tmp/claude-0/q92-cash-runway-planner/indep.py, B_w = B_{w-1} + I*[w > delay] + in_w - C - out_w) matched the engine (tool.mjs) on the defaults (3600, 2200, 2600 ... 6200; low 2,200 in week 2, as the FAQ says), on the README's tax-plus-invoice case (3600, -3800, -3400, -3000, -2600, 1800 ...) and on a 52-week quarterly repeat (landings 2, 15, 28, 41 as the README says; final 6,400, low 4,200). I then applied each suggested move and re-ran the forecast (cases.mjs). The advice is wrong in a reachable case: with cash 1,000, income 1,000 (no delay), costs 1,000, a 1,500 supplier bill in week 2, a 3,000 tax bill and 1,000 grant in week 3 and a 5,000 job in week 7, the page says 'Moving Tax (3,000, week 3) past week 6 closes the gap'. Moving it leaves week 2 at -500. clears (app.mjs:266) only compares the amount with the trough deficit and ignores that a payment landing after the run starts cannot lift the earlier negative weeks. The common case (outflow at or before the run start) is right: moving it to just after the run end recreates the original balance from then on, so no new gap opens. Held at 2 because the 'closes the gap' verdict is the product's headline feature and a user would act on it.
evidence.completeness: Every feature in the README and on the page works end to end in the engine: weekly forecast to 52 weeks, first negative week, the trough, up to 8 one-off rows with half-filled rows refused, repeat interval, per-run shortfall plans with delay and pull-forward, the structural-gap note, CSV with an item column, a share link that round-trips every filled field (more.mjs decode equals input), draft restore that re-opens hidden rows, and opt-in usage counting gated on DNT/GPC. No TODOs or stubs found.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 50/50 pass in about 0.27 s. I seeded 6 mutants with quality_mutate.py and 5 were caught: delay eligibility <= trough changed to <, collection-delay off-by-one, repeat window <= span changed to <, structural > 0 changed to >= 0, and removing the used-outflow dedupe. The boundary clears >= deficit changed to > survived. The test at test.mjs:208 pins the behaviour that is wrong: it asserts that an outflow inside the run is offered, but only in a case where clears is false. No test applies a suggested move and re-runs the forecast, which is how the case-B defect got through.
evidence.craft: I read app.mjs (456 lines), share.mjs, index.html and test.mjs. Pure functions sit apart from the DOM wiring. Item names are escaped before going into innerHTML, storage calls are wrapped in try/catch, share decoding is allowlisted and validated per field, and the comments explain why. Defects: item validation is written twice (checkItems at app.mjs:69 and parseItems at app.mjs:109-124); the CSV quotes item names but does not neutralise a leading '=', so a crafted share link can carry a formula into a downloaded CSV; share.mjs keeps its own copy of MAX_ITEMS as a literal (a test pins the two equal).
evidence.claims: Backed: the defaults' 2,200 low in week 2 (FAQ), the repeat landings 2/15/28/41 (README), the README shortfall example (test.mjs:173 uses cash 3,000 and gets deficit 3,000), nothing uploaded and a fragment-only share link (no fetch in app.mjs; location.hash), disclaimer on the page and in the README, and llms.txt hosts rewritten at deploy (served-copy.mjs: no retired origin left). Not backed: README.md:31 says 'A payment that lands after the shortfall starts is not offered at all', and index.html:108 and when-will-i-run-out-of-cash.html:51 say the delay candidate is 'dated at or before the shortfall starts'. The code (app.mjs:257) offers any outflow up to the trough week, and test.mjs:208 pins that. when-will-i-run-out-of-cash.html:51 also says the pull-forward 'picks the earliest one large enough to matter', but app.mjs:262 picks the earliest whatever its size. The vs-QuickBooks page says the shortfall plan 'says whether it fully closes the gap', which case B contradicts.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an owner of a running service business checking whether the quarterly tax bill makes cash go negative. Entering the five headline numbers and one tax row gives a clear week-by-week answer and a named move, and the CSV and share link make it easy to hand to a bookkeeper. Two problems show up in the first hour. (1) The tool assumes no collections for the first `delay` weeks (the FAQ makes this the headline example), but an ongoing business already has invoices outstanding that will be paid in those weeks. There is no opening-receivables or opening-payables field, so the default forecast understates early cash by up to delay x weekly income (3,600 on the defaults) unless the user adds one-off 'in' rows by hand. (2) Monthly bills must be entered as 'roughly 4' weeks, so a 2,000 monthly rent lands 13 times in 52 weeks (26,000) instead of 12 (24,000).
evidence.domain: Compared against the standard direct-method 13-week cash-flow forecast (opening cash, then receipts from collections of opening and new AR, then disbursements, then the ending balance). The roll-forward matches its arithmetic. Departures: no opening AR or AP schedule (receipts start from zero, as above); a single income stream with one fixed lag, where practitioners age receivables by customer or terms bucket; no calendar-month cadence for monthly bills; and the move-this-payment verdict is checked against the trough amount only, not by re-running the forecast, which is the check a practitioner would make. The structural-gap test (costs > income) is sound and well explained.

defects.what: The delay suggestion says 'closes the gap' whenever the payment's amount is at least the trough deficit, even when the payment lands after the run's first negative week. Moving it cannot lift those earlier weeks. Case B: page says 'Moving Tax (3,000, week 3) past week 6 closes the gap', and after the move week 2 is still -500.

README and both explainer pages say delay candidates are only outflows dated at or before the shortfall starts ('not offered at all' otherwise), but the code offers any outflow up to the trough week and a test pins that; the explainer also says the pull-forward picks the earliest inflow 'large enough to matter', but there is no size filter.

There is no opening receivables or payables input. For an ongoing business the first `collectionWeeks` weeks show zero collections, so early cash is understated by up to delay x weekly income (3,600 on the defaults) and the FAQ's headline example shows a dip that comes from this simplification rather than from the business.
No test applies a suggested move and re-runs the forecast; the clears boundary (>= vs >) mutant survives, and test.mjs:208 pins in-run outflow eligibility only in a case where clears is false.
Monthly bills are entered as 'roughly 4' weeks (FAQ), which lands 13 times per 52 weeks instead of 12, overstating a year of monthly bills by about 8%.
CSV item column is quoted but a name starting with '=' (which a crafted share link can carry) is not neutralised, so spreadsheet apps evaluate it as a formula.
Item validation is duplicated between checkItems and parseItems with slightly different messages.

verdict: The weekly cash roll-forward is right: the defaults, the README's tax-and-invoice case and a 52-week quarterly repeat all match an independent recomputation to the dollar. Share links, CSV and draft restore work as described. It misses the bar on correctness and claims. The product's headline feature, naming the payment whose move 'closes the gap', checks only the payment's size against the trough. For a payment that lands after the shortfall has started it says 'closes the gap' while an earlier week stays negative (case B, week 2 at -500 after the move). The README and both explainer pages describe a stricter rule than the code runs. A bookkeeper would also ask first about opening receivables: the forecast assumes no collections for the first lag weeks, which is not true of a business already trading. Tests are good (50 pass, 5 of 6 mutants caught) but none re-runs the forecast after applying the suggested move.
